context: Affectionate forms: maman, papa (used by adults too).
'Parents' can mean both parents and relatives in general: 'des parents éloignés' = distant relatives.
'Œ' as in 'sœur' sounds like the vowel in 'fur'.
In 'fils' the s is pronounced and the l is silent. 'La fille' also means girl.
Children say papi and mamie (or pépé, mémé).
Similarly: les petits-enfants (grandchildren).
'Tata' and 'tonton' are the affectionate children's words.
The feminine adds -e and the vowel changes: [an] → [een].
'Femme' means both woman and wife; pronounced [FAM], not [FEM].
With 'mon/ma', it usually means boyfriend/girlfriend; 'un copain' can just be a friend.

front: J'ai un frère et deux sœurs.
back: I have one brother and two sisters.
context: In 'deux sœurs' the x is silent before a consonant.
A woman says: 'Je suis fille unique'.

front: Ma sœur aînée habite à Marseille.
back: My older sister lives in Marseille.
context: 'Aîné(e)' = older/eldest; 'cadet(te)' = younger. Also: ma grande sœur, mon petit frère.
'Ton' (your, informal) + masculine noun; 'ta' + feminine; 'tes' + plural.

front: Ma mère et son mari sont très gentils.
pronunciation: [mah mehr ay sohn mah-REE sohn treh zhahn-TEE]
back: My mother and her husband are very kind.
context: 'Son mari' = her husband: son/sa agree with the noun owned, not the owner.
'À la maison' also means at home.
'Faire la cuisine' = to cook.
In France the toilet ('les toilettes', 'les WC') is often in a separate room.
Not 'chamber'! 'Une chambre double' = a double room in a hotel.

front: le salon / la salle de séjour
context: Also 'le séjour'. 'La salle à manger' = dining room.
'Le balcon' = balcony; 'la terrasse' = terrace.
French listings count 'pièces' (rooms, excluding kitchen and bathroom): a T3 or F3 has a living room and two bedrooms.

back: I live on the third floor.
context: In France, the ground floor is 'le rez-de-chaussée', so 'premier étage' is one floor up.

front: Il y a un canapé dans le salon.
pronunciation: [eel yah an kah-nah-PAY dahn luh sah-LOHN]
back: There's a sofa in the living room.
context: 'Il y a' = there is / there are, for singular and plural alike.

front: Le lit est dans la chambre.
back: The bed is in the bedroom.
context: 'Le lit' (bed), 'l'armoire' (wardrobe), 'le bureau' (desk), 'la lampe' (lamp).

front: La table est dans la salle à manger.
pronunciation: [lah TAH-bluh eh dahn lah sal ah mahn-ZHAY]
back: The table is in the dining room.
context: 'Les chaises' = chairs. Many French apartments combine living and dining room.
'Vivre' (to live) is irregular: je vis, tu vis, il vit, nous vivons.
'Famille nombreuse' = large family (officially three or more children in France).
'Une famille recomposée' = a blended family: beau-père (stepfather), belle-mère (stepmother).

front: Viens, je te fais visiter l'appartement.
back: Come, I'll show you around the apartment.
context: 'Faire visiter' = to show someone around. A typical welcome when a guest arrives.
